name: necromancy

attributes.attribute: speaking with or raising the dead
bard who raised a dead hero
dead hero raised to recall lost verses
epic whose lost parts were recovered

sources: Evans-Wentz, W. Y. The Fairy-Faith in Celtic Countries. Gerrards Cross: Colin Smythe Humanities Press, 1911, 151+.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Necromancy is a cosmological concept. It asks whether the Celts spoke with or raised the dead to gather hidden information. Folk tales give witches and fairies this skill, but it is unclear whether ordinary people shared it. Irish texts describe a long rite used by a bard seeking knowledge. The epic Táin Bó Cuailnge had gaps in it. The bard Senchan turned to magic for days to summon the shade of the dead hero Fergus mac Róich. Fergus had joined the cattle raid at the poem's heart. Senchan learned the missing verses and recited them to a gathering of poets, then died from the strain.

okr.objective: necromancy is the Celtic rite of raising the dead for knowledge.
key_results: Necromancy means speaking with or raising the dead.
Witches and fairies held this skill in folk tales.
The bard Senchan raised the hero Fergus mac Róich.
He recovered lost verses of the Táin Bó Cuailnge.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
